subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management removal, should OpenClaw isolate the next DM by rotating/staling the route-matched session and removing the cached Teams conversation reference without deleting transcript files, with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371 as the canonical fix?
rationale: The code path is reviewable, but the durable behavior controls personal-chat history and proactive conversation reachability after app removal, so automation should not choose the retention boundary alone.

options.title: Use non-destructive lifecycle reset
options.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, preserve transcript files, and focus review on the proof-sufficient PR.

options.title: Require stronger deletion semantics
options.body: Block the fix until app removal deletes or archives retained Teams DM transcript/session data under an explicit data-retention policy.

options.title: Defer as platform limitation
options.body: Document Teams local clear-history as not bot-observable and defer lifecycle reset work until maintainers define a broader Teams forget policy.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive lifecycle reset
recommendation.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, preserve transcript files, and focus review on the proof-sufficient PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Teams conversation-store and security-sensitive state history for deciding the retained-history boundary.
